title: NSF Digital Libraries Initiative → Google
summary: The Stanford Integrated Digital Library Project was one of the first six awards of the NSF-led, multi-agency Digital Library Initiative: a $4.5 million NSF cooperative agreement (IRI-9411306) running from September 1994 to August 1999. Larry Page was a graduate student funded under the project, and Sergey Brin, on an NSF graduate fellowship, worked on it; their BackRub prototype ran on equipment paid for by the project and by industry. Page's PageRank patent, owned by Stanford and stating NSF support, was licensed to Google, which was incorporated in September 1998 and raised private venture capital in 1999. The award ran its full course; the research left government through Stanford's standard university licensing, not through the end of the program.

links.claim: Stanford's Office of Technology Licensing licensed PageRank to Google after its incorporation and, as patent holder, ended up with more than 1.8 million Google shares; Google's 1999 funding announcement named Stanford University among its investors.

NSF states that Larry Page was one of the graduate students funded under the NSF-supported DLI project at Stanford, and that Sergey Brin, supported by an NSF Graduate Student Fellowship, also worked on the DLI project.

Brin and Page's 1998 paper describing Google states the research was conducted as part of the Stanford Integrated Digital Library Project, supported by NSF Cooperative Agreement IRI-9411306, with additional funding from DARPA, NASA, Interval Research and the project's industrial partners; NSF says the BackRub prototype's equipment was funded by the DLI project and industrial contributions.

sources.title: The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine

claims.explanation: NSF's Digital Library award paid for Page's graduate work and the BackRub prototype's equipment, and the PageRank patent acknowledges the NSF grant. But Google was a private company incorporated in 1998 and financed by private investors, including a $25 million round led by Sequoia Capital and Kleiner Perkins in 1999; the PageRank patent belongs to Stanford, which licensed it to Google in exchange for equity.

claims.claim: Google was created with CIA or NSA funding.
claims.explanation: The funding acknowledged in Brin and Page's 1998 paper and in the PageRank patent is NSF cooperative agreement IRI-9411306, with co-funding from DARPA, NASA, Interval Research and industrial partners. Neither document acknowledges intelligence-agency funding. Later claims that an intelligence-community research program helped fund Brin's graduate work were not verified from primary records here.
